question: 'Never search' vs embeddings: is the line (a) identity lookup (fetch node N) is never a search, and (b) similarity (what is near this) is a question a tree answers through its own index, which hands back node addresses, so that a search happens only inside a tree and never to resolve an id?
why_it_blocks: born of the answer to open-4cc69605128d
answer: fetch by ID is never a search, it's always a 'go directly there'. our target hardware is 10th gen i7 cpus with 16G RAM and no GPU. so this is the only way it doesn't get bogged down. history: we learned this during the igors when it was taking more than 1 second to read a word into the word graph. i shit you not. 3M entries and the laptop was crawling. that's why we build this row ID model. and it came from Ashton-Tate dbase II of all things. that was the first database i ever used.
